name: symfony/dom-crawler
input_api: new Crawler() then Crawler::addXmlContent(string) (DOMDocument::loadXML with LIBXML_NONET always added); the XML-mode Crawler is traversed with children(), each(), nodeName(), attr(), text() and filterXPath() with namespace discovery and registerNamespace()
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom DOMDocument::loadXML; shared with the standard libxml2 APIs and with sabre/xml
package_own_scope: Crawler XML-mode navigation and query mapping: the addXmlContent default-namespace rewrite check, children()/sibling() element traversal, attr()/text() whitespace normalizing, filterXPath() relativizing, findNamespacePrefixes() and discoverNamespace(). Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity decoding and namespace binding are libxml2.
family: libxml2 via PHP DOMDocument, shared with the standard path and sabre/xml

popularity.caveat: Cumulative package downloads are a package adoption proxy, not XML-specific uses; DomCrawler is mostly installed for HTML crawling and functional tests (symfony/browser-kit, Goutte-style scrapers), so most of these downloads are HTML uses. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path and sabre/xml.

caveats: Crawler's documented default-namespace prefix ('default') resolves to the last default namespace declaration in the document; the order control's <plain xmlns=""> leaves it unbound, so the harness registers default-namespace URIs as ns1, ns2, ... with registerNamespace() and keeps auto-discovery for prefixed names.
addXmlContent replaces every 'xmlns' with 'ns' when the text has no 'xmlns:' prefix declaration; both shared controls declare a prefix, so that rewrite is not exercised.
addXmlContent suppresses libxml errors and yields an empty Crawler for non-well-formed text; only valid controls were run.

name: sabre/xml
input_api: Sabre\Xml\Service::getReader() then Sabre\Xml\Reader::XML(string) and Reader::parse(): builds a Clark-notation {namespace}local element tree with attributes and leaf text (Service::parse also accepts a string or stream resource)
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP XMLReader (Sabre\Xml\Reader extends \XMLReader); shared with the standard XMLReader path
family: libxml2 via PHP XMLReader, shared with the standard XMLReader API

popularity.caveat: Cumulative package downloads are a package adoption proxy, not XML-specific uses; this package shares the libxml2/XMLReader parser family with the standard path.
